questions.title: Mild-to-moderate intestinal amebiasis is treated with metronidazole plus diloxanide furoate
questions.question: A male patient presents with lower abdominal discomfort, flatulence, and occasional diarrhea. A diagnosis of intestinal amebiasis is made, and E histolytica is identified in his diarrheal stools. The preferred treatment that he should have received for the initial symptoms (which were indicative of mild-to moderate disease) is

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diloxanide furoate alone is a luminal agent used to eradicate residual cysts after tissue treatment, or for asymptomatic cyst passers; it is not sufficient alone for symptomatic mild-to-moderate intestinal disease.
explanations.B: Correct. For mild-to-moderate symptomatic intestinal amebiasis, the preferred treatment combines metronidazole (a tissue amebicide that treats the invasive trophozoite infection causing symptoms) with diloxanide furoate (a luminal agent that eradicates any remaining intestinal cysts after the tissue infection is treated). This combination approach ensures both the active tissue infection and the luminal cyst reservoir are cleared, unlike either drug given alone.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Metronidazole alone treats the tissue infection but does not reliably eradicate luminal cysts, risking relapse or continued transmission.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Iodoquinol is a luminal agent, similar in role to diloxanide furoate, but the printed key specifically pairs metronidazole with diloxanide furoate for this scenario.

questions.learning_objective: State that mild-to-moderate symptomatic intestinal amebiasis is treated with metronidazole plus diloxanide furoate together.

questions.title: Hydatid disease does not respond to praziquantel
questions.question: Which helminthic infection does not respond to treatment with praziquantel?

explanations.A: Correct. Hydatid disease, caused by the larval (cyst) stage of Echinococcus granulosus, does not respond reliably to praziquantel; albendazole (often with surgical or percutaneous cyst management) is the standard treatment instead. This is an important exception, since praziquantel is broadly effective against most other trematode and cestode infections, including paragonimiasis, pork tapeworm (Taenia solium) infection and schistosomiasis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Paragonimiasis (lung fluke infection) responds to praziquantel.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pork tapeworm (Taenia solium) infection responds to praziquantel.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Schistosomiasis responds to praziquantel, which is in fact the drug of choice for all Schistosoma species.

questions.learning_objective: State that hydatid disease does not respond to praziquantel, unlike paragonimiasis, pork tapeworm infection or schistosomiasis.

questions.title: Diloxanide furoate treats asymptomatic E histolytica cyst carriage
questions.question: After the acute infection, which of the following medications is given to treat the asymptomatic colonization state of E. histolytica?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Metronidazole is a tissue amebicide for active invasive infection; it does not reliably eradicate the luminal cyst carriage state.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Chloroquine is an antimalarial, not an amebicide used for luminal cyst eradication.
explanations.C: Correct. Diloxanide furoate is a luminal amebicide used to treat the asymptomatic colonization (cyst-passer) state of Entamoeba histolytica after the acute tissue infection has resolved. It clears the intestinal lumen of cysts, preventing relapse or transmission to others. This luminal role is distinct from metronidazole's tissue-amebicide role, so the two drugs are often paired rather than used interchangeably.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Primaquine is an antimalarial that targets liver hypnozoites, not an amebicide for luminal cyst eradication.

questions.learning_objective: State that diloxanide furoate is used to treat the asymptomatic luminal cyst-carriage state of E. histolytica after acute infection.

questions.title: Chloroquine treats acute P vivax attacks but does not eradicate exoerythrocytic forms
questions.question: Which drug should be used for oral treatment of the acute attack of P vivax malaria but does not eradicate exoerythrocytic forms of the parasite?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Mefloquine also acts on blood-stage parasites without eradicating exoerythrocytic (liver hypnozoite) forms, but the printed key specifically names chloroquine as the standard oral treatment for an acute P. vivax attack.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Primaquine is the drug that specifically DOES eradicate exoerythrocytic (liver hypnozoite) forms, the opposite of what this question asks for; it is not the standard treatment for the acute blood-stage attack itself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine is not the standard oral treatment for an acute P. vivax attack.
explanations.D: Correct. Chloroquine is the standard oral treatment for the acute attack of P. vivax malaria, acting on blood-stage (erythrocytic) parasites to resolve the acute illness, but it does not eradicate exoerythrocytic (dormant liver hypnozoite) forms. Because of this, chloroquine treatment for P. vivax must be followed by primaquine to eradicate the hypnozoites and prevent relapse.

questions.learning_objective: State that chloroquine treats the acute blood-stage attack of P. vivax malaria but does not eradicate exoerythrocytic (liver hypnozoite) forms.

questions.title: Severe extraintestinal amebiasis is treated with tinidazole plus diloxanide furoate
questions.question: The drug regimen most likely to be effective in treating severe extraintestinal disease in this patient is:

options.A: Emetine plus diloxanide furoate plus chloroquine

explanations.A: Incorrect. Emetine is an older, more toxic amebicide, not the printed key's preferred regimen for severe extraintestinal disease here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Diloxanide furoate plus iodoquinol combines two luminal agents without a tissue amebicide, insufficient for severe extraintestinal (tissue-invasive) disease.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Chloroquine is an antimalarial, not the primary regimen for severe extraintestinal amebiasis (though it has a historical secondary role in amebic liver abscess unresponsive to other agents).
explanations.D: Correct. Severe extraintestinal amebiasis (such as amebic liver abscess) is effectively treated with tinidazole, a tissue amebicide related to metronidazole, combined with diloxanide furoate to eradicate any residual luminal cysts once the tissue infection is controlled. This mirrors the same tissue-agent-plus-luminal-agent pairing principle used for intestinal disease, adapted for tinidazole's efficacy against extraintestinal (tissue) infection.

questions.learning_objective: State that severe extraintestinal amebiasis is effectively treated with tinidazole plus diloxanide furoate.

questions.title: Malarone manages multidrug-resistant P falciparum in endemic areas
questions.question: Which ONE of the following drugs is efficiently used in management of multidrug-resistant plasmodium falciparum in endemic area?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Chloroquine is ineffective against multidrug-resistant P. falciparum, precisely the setting this question describes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Doxycycline is used as an adjunct or for prophylaxis, but the printed key specifically names Malarone as efficiently managing multidrug-resistant P. falciparum on its own.
explanations.C: Correct. Malarone (atovaquone-proguanil) is efficiently used in the management of multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria in endemic areas. It combines atovaquone's action on the parasite's mitochondrial electron transport chain with proguanil's antifolate activity. Together these two mechanisms give a synergistic effect against strains resistant to older agents such as chloroquine.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Primaquine targets liver hypnozoites and gametocytes; it is not the standard choice for managing multidrug-resistant P. falciparum blood-stage infection.

questions.learning_objective: State that Malarone (atovaquone-proguanil) is efficiently used to manage multidrug-resistant P. falciparum in endemic areas.

questions.title: Mefloquine prophylaxis can still fail against P vivax relapse
questions.question: A traveler in a geographical region where chloroquine-resistant P falciparum is endemic used a drug for prophylaxis but nevertheless developed a severe attack of P vivax malaria. The drug used for prophylaxis was probably:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Atovaquone (as part of Malarone) covers blood-stage parasites broadly and is not the printed key's answer for this scenario.
explanations.B: Correct. Mefloquine is an effective prophylactic choice in chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum regions, but like chloroquine it acts only on blood-stage parasites and does not eradicate P. vivax's dormant liver hypnozoites. A traveller on mefloquine prophylaxis can therefore still develop a P. vivax attack from hypnozoite reactivation after stopping prophylaxis, since mefloquine provides no protection against this relapse mechanism.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Iodoquinol is an amebicide, not an antimalarial prophylactic agent.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Proguanil is typically used in combination (e.g. with atovaquone or chloroquine) rather than as the standalone prophylactic drug the printed key names here.

questions.learning_objective: State that mefloquine prophylaxis does not prevent P. vivax relapse from liver hypnozoite reactivation, since it acts only on blood-stage parasites.
